clue.text: The financial ombudsman limits this material

indicators.note: the limits of something are its boundaries, so only the end letters of each word count

explanation.surface: A financial watchdog sets boundaries on some substance under review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' looks like a verb about regulation, but it asks for the edge letters of the three words before it; 'this material' points back at the clue's own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is the trademarked non-stick coating used on pans, a synthetic polymer substance.

clue.text: Date top Chinese, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: to escort someone out on a date
a further meaning: to kill, slang for eliminating someone
last meaning: a meal bought from a restaurant to eat at home

explanation.surface: Planning an evening with a romantic partner over the best Chinese food in town.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really three meanings: escort on a date, kill (to top someone), and a meal ordered from a restaurant; a Chinese is British for a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese meal is a classic example of food ordered from a restaurant to eat elsewhere, called takeout.

clue.text: Classic location for the mill recommended by dentists

blocks.note: first meaning: the river in George Eliot's novel The Mill on the ...
second meaning: thread for cleaning between teeth

explanation.surface: A literary landmark that dentists happen to endorse.
explanation.walkthrough: The classic is George Eliot's novel The Mill on the Floss, named after a fictional river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Floss is the river beside the mill in Eliot's novel, and dental floss is thread dentists advise patients to use.

clue.text: Trio likes playing — it's a source of energy

indicators.note: musicians playing improvise freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A musical trio enjoys performing, and their music powers them.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking oil means discovering a petroleum deposit, which supplies fuel and therefore power.

clue.text: Information provided by Chesterton, initially?

blocks.note: surface reading: facts supplied by the writer G. K. Chesterton
setter's reading: the writer's initials, G. K., are a common abbreviation for a broad body of facts

explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton was the English author of the Father Brown stories; GK is a standard abbreviation for wide-ranging facts, as in a GK quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means broad factual awareness across many subjects, abbreviated GK, matching the writer's initials.

clue.text: Officer overwhelmed by joy in Highland valley

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so one piece sits wholly inside the other

explanation.surface: A soldier is delighted to find himself in a Scottish glen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelmed by' reads as the officer's emotion, but it places one piece wholly inside the other. Glencoe is a valley in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Glencoe is a famous glen in the Scottish Highlands, site of the 1692 massacre.

clue.text: Rover is leading name of most Alsatian dogs

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its front, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Rover is said to be the most common name given to German shepherd dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like a dog's name, fitting the Alsatians, but it means a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who wanders from place to place, which is what a nomad does.

clue.text: Acceptable building extension for conservative types?

blocks.note: an extension added to a building

explanation.surface: An approved annexe planned for a building used by traditionalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives sit on the political right, so right-wing describes people of that persuasion.

clue.text: Elvis plied regularly with special kind of fats

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Elvis kept himself supplied with a particular type of greasy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the class of organic compounds that includes fats, oils and waxes.

clue.text: Editor bleeps second half out, making it suitable for consumption

indicators.note: putting half a word out removes those letters, here its back three

explanation.surface: An editor censors offensive material to make a broadcast fit for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible describes food fit to be eaten, safe and palatable to consume.

clue.text: See 4
Attack leading study  …

blocks.note: ahead, as a team is up by a goal

explanation.surface: The ellipses chain this into one sentence about an assault and a fixed charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is informal British for revising or cramming a subject intensively.

clue.text: …  concerning fixed charge  …

explanation.surface: Part of a chained sentence that seems to be about a set fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a price but is the military sense, a rush at an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack, the same as a charge at an enemy.

clue.text: …  that's obsolete after support is revised retrospectively

indicators.note: coming after means placed behind, fixing which piece is written second

explanation.surface: An outdated fee is changed to apply from an earlier date once financial support arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Backdated describes something made effective from an earlier time, like a pay rise applied to past months.

clue.text: Talk about when to drive off in the late afternoon

indicators.note: talk means speech, so the phrase is identified by how it is said

blocks.note: the booked slot for starting a round of golf

explanation.surface: Discussing the right moment to leave by car later in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive off' sounds like leaving in a car, but it is golf: the first stroke is driven off a tee at an allotted time.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime is the part of the day, around four to six, when afternoon tea or an early meal is taken.

clue.text: Showing interest initially in distribution of cheap tat? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Showing interest initially in distribution of cheap tat? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter is used
distribution spreads things around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shows keen interest as cheap junk is handed out, or rather does not.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into the mixed letters of CHEAP TAT; the whole clue, with 'Quite the opposite' flipping 'Showing interest', is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means lacking enthusiasm or concern, the reverse of being keen or engaged.

clue.text: Sign reversed by top Greek mathematician  …

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: A top Greek mathematician turns a sign around, part of a chained sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Alexandrian scholar whose Elements founded classical geometry.

clue.text: Encourage secretive group that is hiding tax

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: id est, the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Urging on a shadowy sect that dodges its tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax; 'that is' gives the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate a quality or relationship is to foster and nurture it, which is to encourage it.

clue.text: …  providing clear evidence of invention

blocks.note: first meaning: obvious, plain to see
second meaning: the official document granting rights to an inventor

explanation.surface: The end of a chained sentence in which someone supplies solid proof of a new device.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means obvious; as a noun it is the licence protecting a new invention.

clue.text: Papers have problems supporting this leader

indicators.note: the leader is the one in front, so only the first letter is taken
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, setting the order of the pieces

explanation.surface: Newspapers have trouble backing the current party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' looks like newspapers but means soft paper hankies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissues are thin, soft sheets of paper used as handkerchiefs or for wrapping.

clue.text: Drop support for scapegoat

blocks.note: a rope that braces a tent or mast

explanation.surface: Abandoning one's backing for someone who has been blamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is a person made to take the blame for others, exactly a scapegoat.

clue.text: Chapel is so fortunate to hold returned relic

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, running across their boundaries
returned means sent back, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: letters spanning chapel, is, so and fortunate

explanation.surface: A chapel feels lucky to keep an old sacred object brought back to it.
explanation.walkthrough: A relic sounds like a saint's bones in the chapel, but here it is an ancient remain in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient organism, a relic of the distant past.

clue.text: Terribly frosty around November? They keep nuts warm

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled
around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

explanation.surface: A bitterly cold late-autumn month calls for something to keep the squirrels' food stores warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs; 'nuts' is slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's underpants, which cover and warm the testicles, jokingly called nuts.

clue.text: Without borders, fancy short stop at sea

indicators.note: without borders means the edges are stripped away, leaving the inner letters

explanation.surface: A daydream about briefly halting a voyage on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor is to moor a vessel by dropping a heavy hook, halting it on the water.

clue.text: Is nothing sacred to them?

blocks.note: surface reading: the indignant cry of someone shocked by irreverence
setter's reading: people for whom literally nothing is sacred, rejecting all values

explanation.walkthrough: The stock outraged phrase is taken literally: these people really do hold nothing sacred. Latin nihil means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihilists reject all moral and religious principles, believing life is without meaning or value.

clue.text: Old school punishment excited silent majority

indicators.note: the majority is most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional classroom penalty stirred the usually quiet majority into protest.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines were a punishment in British schools: writing the same sentence out many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils given lines had to copy a sentence repeatedly, a classic old-fashioned school penalty.

clue.text: Conclude there's no escaping hell

indicators.note: something escaping gets out and leaves, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: Deciding that once you are damned there is no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, so it means to conclude.

clue.text: Chance taken by father holding position

indicators.note: holding means grasping inside, so one piece contains the other

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the way something lies, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A priest takes a gamble while keeping his post.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a flier is an idiom for making a speculative bet or risky attempt.

clue.text: Proposition discovered left out in hotel chain

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so one letter disappears from the chain's name

explanation.surface: A proposal is found to have been missed at a well-known hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings, make advances to and stumbled upon, sit alongside the wordplay: the hotel group's name without L.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on someone is to make a sexual advance, a proposition; to hit on an idea is to discover it.

clue.text: Dumping of waste into a ruin is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not as it should be, so the letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Fly-tipping rubbish into an old ruined building is an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Urination is the discharge of liquid bodily waste, a cheeky reading of dumping waste.

clue.text: Their colour discrimination makes rodents hold back like this

definitions.note: describes the people by what they practise

indicators.note: back means turned in the opposite direction, so the short phrase runs right to left
to hold is to keep inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: Telling colours apart is what lets rodents keep restrained in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is the Latin word printed after a quoted error to mean 'thus, as written'.
explanation.definitionFit: Racists are people who discriminate against others because of their skin colour or race.

clue.text: Bride's gone berserk, making bits and pieces

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A furious bride smashes things up at her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris means scattered fragments and remains, the odds and ends left after destruction.
